item.title: Martin Institute Seeks Student Media Ambassador
item.description:
The Media Ambassador will work directly with the Martin Institute Media Director Emily Drew to capture and share the stories of the Martin Institute across programs and events. The Ambassador will produce engaging multimedia content and help run the Martin Institute’s official social media channels. This role is ideal for students with experience in journalism, marketing, communications, or digital media production.

Martin Institute Student Ambassadors are a select cohort of student leaders who help shape and advance the Institute's work across the Davidson College community. As ambassadors, students serve as connectors, collaborators, and changemakers who bring ideas to life, engage their peers, and help foster a campus culture dedicated to leadership, civic engagement, and the public good. Each Ambassador partners with one of the Institute's Program Area Directors to support innovative programs, conduct research, develop new initiatives, and engage students in meaningful conversations and experiences. While each Ambassador contributes to a specific program area, the cohort works together to advance the Martin Institute's mission and strengthen connections across its five program areas. Student Ambassadors play an essential role in ensuring that the Institute's work is informed by student perspectives, responsive to emerging issues, and connected to the broader Davidson community.

Key Responsibilities

  • Event Coverage: Attend assigned campus events and activities to gather photos, short-form video, and interviews.
  • Content Creation: Draft compelling captions, design digital assets (via Canva or Adobe Express), and produce high-quality short video content tailored for Facebook, Instagram, LinkedIn, and YouTube.
  • Social Media Management: Work with the Media Director to schedule posts and monitor engagement.
  • Story Pitching: Participate in weekly editorial meetings with the Media Director to brainstorm new content series, feature stories and profiles, and event coverage schedules.
  • Media Archiving: Organize, tag, and upload event photos and video assets to the Institute’s shared media library.

Qualifications

  • Strong written and verbal communication skills with a keen eye for storytelling.
  • Hands-on experience creating social content (ideally on Instagram, YouTube, and/or Canva).
  • Basic photography and smartphone video editing skills (such as with CapCut, Reels).
  • Comfortable interviewing peers, faculty, and campus guests on camera.
  • Organized, proactive, and able to work independently during scheduled event coverage.
  • Curious, dependable, eager to learn.
  • Strong communicators who enjoy connecting with people and building community.
  • Excited to help build and strengthen one of Davidson's signature interdisciplinary institutes.

Bonus Qualifications

  • Experience with Adobe Creative Cloud (Lightroom, Premiere Pro, Photoshop).
  • Knowledge of AP Style or basic journalism standards.
  • Longform video or podcast experience.
  • Interested in a career or advanced degree in Communications, Journalism, Marketing, Film, or a related field.

Additional Information:

  • Expected Time Commitment:  8-10 hours per week, occasional evening hours 
  • Employment Dates: October 2026 - May 7, 2027
  • Reports to:  Martin Institute Media Director Emily Drew

Interested individuals should send a cover letter describing your interest and resume to contact@example.edu and contact@example.edu no later than October 8th at 5pm.

item.title: Applications for Spring ‘27 Section of XPL 199 Due October 27th and then Rolling if Space Allows
item.description:
The course XPL 199 - High Impact Experiential Learning - allows you to engage in personal, professional, cultural, and academically relevant experiences with corporations or nonprofits organizations for academic credit.  In addition to working with a host organization for 8 - 10 hours a week, students attend a weekly seminar to reflect on their experiences in relation to course readings, share critical learning moments, complete course assignments, and seek peer guidance.  The class seminar meets in-person on Fridays at 1:30pm in addition to other meetings and activities.  

Interested in taking XPL 199 in the Spring 2027?  You must apply by completing this brief google form no later than October 27th at 5pm.  Instructors will notify you by October 29th to let you know if you have been accepted into the course so that you can add it to your webtree and have sufficient time to apply for internships/opportunities if you don't already have a position secured. Students can be added to the course / waitlist after the initial March 30 deadline and will be let into the course as space is available. 

While the Matthews Center for Career Development (MCCD) and the Center for Civic Engagement (CCE) offer resources to help you, each student is responsible for finding an internship, service or project-based opportunity. Internships must be completed with an established, legally recognized organization that provides a structured, professional environment; a qualified supervisor; and substantive, field-related work aligned with course learning outcomes. Internships with informal groups, unregistered businesses, current students, or close friends/family members do not meet requirements.  In addition, host organizations must adhere to the guidelines established by the Mathews Center for Career Development at Davidson College.

Timeline:

  • October 27 - Deadline to apply for permission to XPL 199 using this google form.  Note that you must have friday afternoons at 1:30pm available on your course schedule for the seminar.
  • October 29- Instructor will let you know  if you have permission or if you are on the waitlist,  Those granted permission can add the course to their webtree.
  • Nov 3- Webtree closes at 5pm.  Enter your course preferences on webtree and include XPL 199 if you have been given permission. The course reference number is . You can put the course last on your webtree if you have been given permission to enroll.
  • Nov 6 -  - January 15 - Work with instructor to secure an internship if you do not have one.  Opportunities will be posted through the Center for Civic Engagement and the Matthews Center for Career Development.
  • January 19- Internships, projects, or service placements must be finalized by this date and you must be ready to begin the internship the first week of classes.

item.description:
APPLYING FOR A SOCIAL SECURITY NUMBER

Are you an F-1 student that recently got hired? If so, you need a Social Security Number (SSN)! You’ll need to apply for an SSN and then sign up for a spot on one of ISE's upcoming Social Security Administration (SSA) trips. Please review the instructions and information below in preparation for your trip. 

  1. Complete the online application for a SSN, following the instructions and advice outlined on the ISE website. Write down your SSN Application Reference Number (it will begin with the letter “O”) 
    • *If you are not yet 18 years old, you will not be able to complete the online application. If you cannot complete the online application, please print out and complete the SS-5 form from this website to do a paper application.
    • Screenshot your application reference number when you complete the application. Once you exit this screen, you will not be able to revisit the page or find the reference number. 
  2. Sign up on WildcatSync for a space on an ISE trip to the Social Security Administration.  
    • Since you’ll be with our Davidson College group and group appointments are already scheduled, please do NOT make an appointment at the conclusion of your SSN online application. We are offering the following trips to the SSA this semester:
      • Wednesday, September 16 (1:30-4:30pm) 
      • Tuesday, September 22 (11am-2pm) *Fall Break option
      • Thursday, October 1 (11am-2pm) 
      • Tuesday, October 27 (11am-2pm). 
  3. Gather your documents (*must be printed, physical versions) 
    • I-20 (NOT a copy)
    • I-94 (Arrival/Departure record)
    • Passport
    • Your Application Reference Number (Begins with the letter “O”). *You must complete the online Social Security Number Application BEFORE your visit. 
    • Employment letter (DOCX)
      • Send to your supervisor to complete the top portion. If you have multiple jobs on campus, just choose one of your supervisors to complete the form.
      • Then email to Event Contact, Event Contact, or Event Contact for an ISE/DSO signature.
      • All signatures can be digital.
  4. Meet at the Alvarez College Union Parking Lot on your Appointment Day: We will need to depart promptly at the scheduled departure time for the Concord Social Security Administration Office. For trips departing at 11am, please meet at the Union Parking Lot by 10:45am. We aim to arrive back on campus by 2pm. For trips departing at 1:30pm, please meet at the Union Parking Lot by 1:15pm. We aim to arrive back on campus by 4:30pm. 

You will receive an email reminder closer to the trip confirming your spot on the van. Should your plans change and you are no longer able to go, please inform Event Contact (contact@example.edu) so that another student may be able to take your space. 

AFTER YOU’VE APPLIED/RECEIVED YOUR SSN

Receiving your Social Security Number (SSN) via Mail

  • If not provided at your visit, the Social Security Administration (SSA) will send you a receipt notice within 3-4 business days of your visit confirming they have received all of your materials. 
  • You should receive your Social Security Number (SSN) in the mail 10-15 days after receiving the receipt. All mail will be sent to your on-campus mailing address. 
  • When your mail arrives to campus, you will receive a mail notification to your inbox. Please be on the lookout for this email so that you can promptly pick up your mail from Social Security. 

Reporting your SSN to Davidson College Human Resources (HR)

  • Once you have received your Social Security Card, please make sure to update your records with HR.
  • Visit the HR office on campus with your Social Security card. No appointment is necessary. HR is open from 8:30am-12:30pm and 1:30pm-5pm on weekdays for walk-ins. The HR Office is located in the little houses behind Wall at Jackson Court #11. 
  • You must report your SSN to HR in order to continue working in your position. You can begin/continue working in your position prior to having your SSN secured. 

Adding your SSN to Sprintax Calculus

  • Once you have received your SSN, you need to add it to your Sprintax Calculus profile.
  • Log in to your Sprintax Calculus account. 
    • Click “Log In with your institution account” at the very bottom
    • Find Davidson College
    • Login with your Davidson username and password.
  • Locate the section for “Personal Data:” Find the area within your account where you can update your personal details, including your U.S. tax identification number.
  • Enter your SSN: Input your SSN in the appropriate field.
  • Save the changes: Be sure to save the updated information to ensure it's reflected in your Sprintax Calculus account.

Adding your SSN to Sprintax Tax Returns (*if you receive your SSN during tax filing season in the spring)

  • In the “About You” section of Sprintax Tax Prep, find the question “Do you have a US tax identification number (ITIN/SSN)?”
  • Select “Yes” and enter your SSN in the corresponding field

Protecting your SSN

  • Your Social Security Number is yours for life and is considered sensitive information. 
  • Keep your Social Security card in a safe place and never share it via email.

Merging your ITIN and SSN (*Only applicable to students that already previously received an ITIN)

  • If you have an Individual Tax Identification Number (ITIN), you are required to notify the IRS that you now have a Social Security Number so that they can merge your accounts and close your ITIN. Instructions can be found at the bottom of the IRS’ ITIN website under the heading “If you get a Social Security Number.”

Troubleshooting if you do not receive your SSN 

  • According to the SSA’s FAQ website, if you do not receive your SSN within 3 weeks of visiting the office, you should contact the SSA. 
  • ISE recommends contacting the SSA office where you applied for your SSN, likely the Concord SSA. You can contact the Concord SSA office at 555-555-0100 during their business hours: Monday - Friday from 9am-4pm. 
  • When calling to request an update on your application, make sure to have your application reference number, the date of your visit, and your personal identification information available so they can look up your information. 
  • If they instruct you to come back to the SSA for a follow up visit, please check in with ISE about upcoming trips to the SSA or go ahead and arrange a follow up visit on your own.

Call for proposals - The Davidson Fund for Racial Equity is available during the Academic Year AND Summer! 

What is it and what does it provide? 

  • The Davidson Fund for Racial Equity provides support for students to explore questions of racial equity through meaningful internships, research experiences, and civic engagement opportunities during the academic year and summer break.  We are accepting applications on a rolling basis until March 30th at 11:59pm. 
  • Grant requests for the academic year can be up to $3,500 and up to $4,000 for research experiences involving faculty mentors.
  • Grant requests for summer 2027 can be up to $4,500 and up to $5,000 for research experiences involving faculty mentors. 
  • For proposals involving research - Consistent with other research-focused granting programs across campus, students must have a faculty mentor who offers advice and feedback on the independent project.  The faculty advisor will receive a $500 stipend and students should add this to their proposed budget making the maximum proposed grant $4,000 (and $5,500 for summer). Any research request related to the college’s history will be reviewed by the Standing Committee on Race and Slavery.

Get Involved

Together, let’s celebrate, uplift, and support our Hispanic and Latinx communities!

item.title: TimelyCare Raffle
item.description:
Join TimelyCare by November 13th to enter a raffle & get access to free health and wellbeing resources! 

TimelyCare is a virtual health and wellbeing service that provides support for all Davidson students!

Sign up now: timelycare.davidson.edu 

Join TimelyCare to get access to: 

TalkNow: 24/7 on-demand virtual access to support from behavioral health professionals for a wide range of concerns. From feeling down or stressed, to relationship concerns, crisis situations, and more, someone is available to talk. Talk Now is available wherever you are: here at Davidson, while at home, and abroad. 

Health Coaching: Access support from a health coach or nutritional specialist for support developing healthy habits and  behaviors (sleep habits, time management, mindfulness, nutrition support, and more).

Self-Care Content: 24/7 access to self-care tools and resources, such as meditation and yoga sessions, helpful videos, and short articles from experts.

Basic Needs Support: Not all barriers to success for students are in the classroom, or even on campus. Basic Needs Support helps students stay on track with their academic goals by connecting them to free or reduced-cost community resources.

Newsletter (Week of 9/14/2026)

Prehealth Events:  

THIS WEEK:

  • Pre-PA Society Information Session, Sep. 14, 7:30 pm, Union 209
    • All are welcome, no matter your class year or how much information you know about the pre-PA path. Discussions will include: he physician assistant career, the pre-PA path at Davidson, and how Pre-PA Society can help along the way. Light snacks will be provided, come with questions and bring your friends!
  • Healthcare Network Reception with Students/Alumni, Sep. 15, 6 – 7 PM, Union Lobby
    • A networking reception immediately preceding the Fall Research Symposium. Meet with alumni in the healthcare profession. Establish potentially valuable relationships with alumni (such as shadowing!), ask questions to learn about their experiences, and potentially land connections that will help you on your professional journey! Register in advance on Handshake by Sep. 9th. All are welcome! 
  • Prehealth Programs Sophomore Meeting, Sep. 16, 7:30 pm, Wall 210
    • Meeting for sophomores in prehealth programs to get reacquainted with the program, receive updates and resources and discuss what is needed to be a competitive applicant. 
  • Resumania, Sep. 16, 10 AM – 3 PM, Union Atrium
    • Meet one-on-one with a career adviser from the Matthews Center for Career Development. Bring your resume (it doesn’t have to be perfect!) and with the expertise of a career adviser you will learn exactly what employers are looking for, what makes them toss a resume in the "no" pile, and understand how to bypass the robots and grab a human's attention (critical in today's AI climate).
  • Award - The Premedicine and Allied Health Professions Program Awards are presented annually to outstanding juniors (class of 2028) pursuing medicine. To be considered for the Sandy Black Memorial Award or the Daniela Blain Woods Award complete the following form. You will be asked to submit a statement and upload a resume. Apply here, deadline is January 31, 2027
  • The 2026-2027 PAC Student Application is now open and due by Nov. 1st. Find it here, make a copy, and complete by due date. 

UPCOMING: (tip: add to your calendar now so you can plan ahead)

  • In person - Personal Statement Writing Workshop, Oct. 7, 7:30 pm, Wall 320
    • Personal Statement Writing Workshop for students applying to health professional programs and/or 2026-2027 PAC Evaluation. This is an in-person writing workshop - please bring your laptop.
  • Virtual - Personal Statement Writing Workshop, Oct. 14, 6:00 pm, Zoom
    • Personal Statement Writing Workshop for students applying to health professional programs and/or 2026-2027 PAC Evaluation.
  • How to Finance Medical School, Oct. 28, 7:30 pm, Wall 320
    • “Financing Your Medical Education & Understanding New Federal Loan Regulations" by Penny Greenwood, Office of Financial Aid/Medical Education, Wake Forest Medical School. Open to all students. 

Additional Opportunities and Events:

  • The nominations for the 2027-2029 American Society for Clinical Investigation (ASCI) Postbaccalaureate Fellowship Award are open and deadline is soon. 
    • The 2027-2029 ASCI Postbaccalaureate provides an intensive, two-year mentored laboratory research experience in an ASCI member lab. This is an excellent gap year opportunity for students interested in academic medicine and research. Any member in good standing may serve as nominator.
  • Wake Forest Pathways to Possibility: Transforming Medical Education for the Future, Sep. 12, Wake Forest University School of Medicine.
    • Opportunity for junior and senior students interested in health professions (including optometry, dentistry, nursing, veterinary, allied health, allopathic, osteopathic medicine, etc.) Recruiters and pathway program leaders from health profession schools and programs look forward to meeting with over 300 students each year. Register to attend here here. 
  • NEW: Info session about the Master of Science in Physician Assistant Studies (PAS) program at MUSC, Sep. 16, 10 am. Join to learn more about the Master of Science in PA studies program. Program faculty will discuss the program's curriculum, admissions requirements, the application process, and what sets MUSC apart from other universities. You will also have an opportunity to ask any questions you might have. Register here.
  • Let's Capture Summer Research: CV Writing Workshop, Sep. 29, Common Hour, location TBD
    • Don't have a CV, not sure where to begin or maybe you'd just like some advice on strengthening what you have? Join Aisling Zaccarelli from the Matthews Center for a CV Writing Workshop that provides detailed explanations, as well as step-by-step processes for creating an effective CV for graduate school or professions in STEM/Medicine. 
  • NeuroNight Fall Edition 2026, Sep. 30, 5:30 pm, Mauzé Family Terrace 
    • A social gathering of Davidson’s Neuroscience Program and Club members. Great opportunity to meet students and professors excited about neuroscience and learn about opportunities on campus. 
  • North Carolina Public Health Association Conference, Sep. 30, 7:30 AM – 4 PM, Concord
    • Join Aisling Zaccarelli in the Matthews Center for Career Development for the first day of the 2026 North Carolina Public Health Association Fall Educational Conference. This year's conference will be held in Concord, NC. We will depart campus at 7:45 in the Union parking lot and return by 4pm. Davidson's Department of Public Health will cover the cost of your registration and your transportation to/from the event. Lunch will be provided. All students who plan to attend will need to speak with their professors in advance to let them know that you will be missing class. Additionally, all students who plan to attend are required to attend a pre-departure meeting on Monday, September 14 from 4:30-5:15pm in the Matthews Center. Sign up and make some incredible connections while learning a ton!
  • Free CE Event 10/11: Modern Zoonoses & Emerging Disease Threats, Oct 11, NC State CVM 
    • Sign up using this link as it is first-come, first-served and its capped. 
  • 2027 MCAT Registration will open Oct. 20-22. Registration opens by testing center location. Sign up to receive announcements on registration and the testing year here. A webinar for examinees will be held on Oct. 6 at 3 pm ET, register for the webinar here. The AAMC Fee Assistance Program is also open. 
  • Chart Your Path: The Experiential Learning Program Fair, Oct.6, common hour, Union Atrium 
    • Catalyst is hosting "Chart Your Path": The Experiential Learning Program Fair where you can: Find experiential learning opportunities & resources; Connect with internship, research, fellowship, and study-away leaders from across campus; Map your experiential learning path for 2026 and beyond; Explore funding opportunities & grant writing tips
  • Medical Education Development Program at the UNC School of Medicine Open House, Sat. Oct.17 at UNC-Chapel Hill
    • Prospective students and pre-health advisors are invited to join on campus to meet Medical Education Development (MED) Program at the UNC School of faculty, leadership, and alumni and learn more about the MED experience.
  • What’s Next? Pre-Health & Science Bridge Year Pathways, Oct. 27, Common Hour, location TBD
    • Have you been working on your PAC application this past week and realized that you might need or want to take an extra year or two before applying to gain experience? Or perhaps you already know that you want to take some after graduation before heading into a graduate/professional degree program? If you're thinking about or know that you need some additional experience, but aren't sure exactly what that could look like, this program is for you. We'll cover a range of options and hear from a few young alumni who are in their bridge year experience. You'll learn about the different types of experiences that will make your application even stronger, as well as learn factors to consider when making a decision. 
  • NC Missions of Mercy (NC MOM) Clinic, Oct. 31, Levine Health Services Center 
    • Register to volunteer here and visit the NC Dental Society Foundation for more info. 
  • Pre-Health Shadowing: The "How To" Guide, Nov. 10, common hour, Wall 210
    • Learn how to effectively network and be able to have conversations with people you don't know in your field of study. Additionally, you'll learn how to identify and reach out to people to request shadowing opportunities in pre-health. We'll go over networking etiquette and tools you can use. 
  • UIW Rosenberg School of Optometry Virtual Info Session, Nov. 18, 12 pm, Zoom
    • This presentation is designed for pre-optometry students, undergraduate students, recent graduates, and anyone interested in pursuing a career in optometry. Whether you're exploring healthcare professions or preparing to apply to optometry school, this session will provide valuable insights into UIWRSO Doctor of Optometry program and the path to becoming an eye care professional.

    • The Goldwater Summer Research Internship Program is a 10-week research opportunity in Chemistry, CISE, Engineering, Life Sciences, or Physics and Astronomy at academic and national laboratories across the U.S. Each project is managed independently and may have different eligibility criteria, schedules, expectations, and costs. Each intern will receive $10,500 to cover the internship and internship-related expenses. Link to application.
